Taches
TATCH-ez
noun
From Old French tache, a fastening or clasp; rendering Hebrew qeres, the hooks or clasps of gold and brass that coupled the tabernacle curtains into one.

📖 Biblical Definition

Taches are the clasps by which the curtains of the tabernacle were coupled together — fifty of gold for the inner curtains of fine linen, and fifty of brass for the tent of goats’ hair above. The LORD’s own word gives their purpose: “thou shalt make fifty taches of gold, and couple the curtains together with the taches: and it shall be one tabernacle” (Exo 26:6). Ten separate breadths of embroidered work, wrought by many hands, were made ONE dwelling by these small fastenings; without the taches there were curtains, but no tabernacle. The gold clasps stood at the join of the two great sets of curtains, directly over the place of the veil, so that the line of union ran above the way into the holiest. Small things carried the unity of the whole house of God. Let the believer read the lesson the apostle draws for the true tabernacle, the Church: the body is “fitly joined together and compacted by that which every joint supplieth” (Eph 4:16). The saints are many breadths of diverse weaving, but Christ couples them into one dwelling of God through the Spirit; and the humble members that bind brother to brother are as the taches of gold — little seen, yet bearing the oneness of the whole.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

The gold and brass clasps that coupled the tabernacle curtains, making many breadths one dwelling.

expand to see more

TACHES, the clasps or fastenings by which the curtains of the tabernacle were coupled.

Fifty of gold joined the inner curtains of fine twined linen; fifty of brass the tent of goats’ hair.

By them the many breadths became one tabernacle, as the LORD commanded.

They stood at the great join of the curtains, over against the veil.

They figure the hidden bonds by which Christ makes His many people one house of God.

📖 Key Scripture

Exo 26:6 — "And thou shalt make fifty taches of gold, and couple the curtains together with the taches: and it shall be one tabernacle."

Exo 26:11 — "And thou shalt make fifty taches of brass, and put the taches into the loops, and couple the tent together, that it may be one."

Exo 39:33 — "And they brought the tabernacle unto Moses, the tent, and all his furniture, his taches, his boards, his bars, and his pillars, and his sockets,"

Eph 4:16 — "From whom the whole body fitly joined together and compacted by that which every joint supplieth, according to the effectual working in the measure of every part, maketh increase of the body unto the edifying of itself in love."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

A fastening of the sanctuary, not a contested doctrine; it recovers the weight of small, hidden things that carry the unity of the house of God.

expand to see more

Taches face no postmodern redefinition. The truth they carry rebukes the love of the conspicuous: the age honours the embroidered breadths — the visible, the platformed, the admired — and despises the small clasps that no visitor ever praised, though without them there was no tabernacle at all.

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is the honour of the hidden bond. God specified the taches as exactly as the cherubim, for the unity of His house hung upon them. So in the Church, the unnoticed members who couple brother to brother — the peacemakers, the intercessors, the faithful joints of supply — bear a weight of glory out of all proportion to their size.

🔗 Greek & Hebrew Roots

From the Old French for a clasp, taches render the Hebrew qeres, the fifty gold and fifty brass fastenings that made the tabernacle one.

Taches — Old French tache, a fastening; Hebrew qeres.

They figure the hidden bonds that make Christ’s people one house.
